title: Web security
goal: Recognise common trust boundaries and basic defences.
explanation: XSS happens when untrusted content is treated as executable page content. Use safe text insertion and context-appropriate output handling; do not inject arbitrary HTML.
SQL injection mixes user data with query syntax. Use parameterised queries, least-privilege database access and server-side authorisation. Input validation alone is not a substitute for binding.

CSRF can abuse automatically attached credentials to trigger unwanted actions. Apply appropriate anti-CSRF tokens and origin checks for state-changing requests, alongside cookie settings. Never put credentials in source control or client bundles.
exercise: Review a small form: identify one XSS risk, one server validation requirement and the authorisation check.
hint: Treat input as data and enforce permissions on the server.

quiz.question: Which defence directly addresses SQL injection in values?
quiz.explanation: Parameters separate values from executable SQL. Additional access controls still matter.
